mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which signals a potential economic downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a supply-side contraction, which can lead to lower corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of industrial production decline.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong consumer spending, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increase > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of low unemployment and strong payroll growth.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts by more than 10% in a month indicates a strong demand for housing, which boosts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of increased housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of high interest rates and rising inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures by more than 1% in a month signals weakening consumer demand, which can lead to lower corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of declining personal consumption expenditures.
